concept.title: Tables
concept.abstract: This section covers the Table style in DOCX — the primary structure for presenting information with inherent row-and-column relationships — and ten scenarios: a standard multi-column table, a table with a caption, a table with no header row, merged cells, nested tables, lists and images inside table cells, tables spanning multiple pages, consecutive tables, and a two-column parameter table in a reference topic. The converter reads each table's structure, cell complexity, and topic context to determine whether to map it to <simpletable>, a CALS <table>, or <properties>.

conbody.p: ATable is the primary structure for reference and lookup content. It is a structural mechanism to present information that has inherent row-and-column relationships — parameter names and their values, feature names and their states, error codes and their meanings, API fields and their data types.

A table reduces a lookup task from reading a paragraph to scanning a row and column. In DITA-XML, a table is structured data — each cell is a discrete, addressable unit that a transform can reformat for PDF, or online help output, filter by column for conditional publishing, and extract independently for reuse in other deliverables.

In a .docx file, a table is inserted through Insert → Table and can include a header row, merged cells, and a Caption-styled paragraph. A parameter table typically has a header row and no merged cells. A table with merged cells usually spans a label across several rows and/or columns.

The converter reads the table's XML to determine row count, column count, and merge spans, then routes the output to either <simpletable> or a CALS <table> + <tgroup> structure — and where a two-column table appears inside a Reference topic with columns corresponding to property names and values, it maps to <properties> instead.
The following table lists the table structures and their corresponding DITA output:

row.entry: Simple rows and columns without merged cells
Complex tables with merged cells or structured layouts
Name–value pairs, configuration settings, parameters, or attribute lists

conbody.note: A table simulated with tabs, spaces, or a screenshot produces no table element in the output. Always insert tables using Insert → Table.
